title: Normalized condensed-module pullback tensor comparison
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $f:X\to Y$ a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Use the coefficient rings $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], module inverse image [def-sfb-module-upper-star], the ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and their relative tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Write $r=f^*$ using the canonical inverse-coefficient transport of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction]. Define the ordinary tensor comparison $t_{M,N}:r(M\otimes_{B_Y}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}rM\otimes_{B_X}rN$ by the unique balanced-generator equation: the abelian inverse-image tensor map followed by inverse image of the balanced quotient and $t$ is the balanced quotient of the pulled-back modules. Define its derived comparison $t^D_{K,L}:D(r)(K\otimes^L L)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(r)K\otimes^L D(r)L$ as the unique family natural in both variables with the following representative normalization. For every pair of cochain complexes $A,B$, the ordinary comparisons on the summands indexed by $p+q=n$ give a chain map $d:r(A\otimes B)\to rA\otimes rB$, and $D(r)(\mu_Q)\,\mathrm{fac}_{A\otimes B}\,Q(d)=t^D_{QA,QB}(\mathrm{fac}_A\otimes\mathrm{fac}_B)\mu_Q$, with composition read from left to right. Here $\mu_Q:QA\otimes^L QB\to Q(A\otimes B)$ is the specified lax tensor comparison of localization and fac is the exact-functor factorization. The identification of r with the extension-of-scalars upper star is restriction along the inverse of the canonical coefficient isomorphism; small colimits are obtained by universe shrinking, and complexes use the existing total relative tensor structure.

proof.text: The ordinary balanced-generator comparison is the inverse monoidal constraint of the module inverse-image functor r. Its degreewise total-complex comparison is therefore mapBifunctorComparison of the oplax monoidal constraint: both satisfy the same equations on every tensor summand. Their equality follows from the already proved uniqueness of the total-complex map.

Apply inverseImageModule_preservesFlat to r, using the inverse of the canonical coefficient isomorphism. The support pullback adjunction makes r a left adjoint. Together with the existing exactness and monoidal instances, these are the hypotheses of the source-library leftDerivedTensorComparison theorem. Transport that isomorphism from the total left derived functor to the termwise exact derived functor by leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Naturality follows by conjugating the source comparison naturality square.

The characterizing homotopy-category square for leftDerivedTensorComparison commutes with the exact-functor isomorphism by leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory_hom_app_fac. Apply it to the homotopy classes of two complexes. The localization tensor map for Q is the map for Qh on those classes, and the homotopy factorization maps agree with the complex factorization maps. Substitute the total-complex identification from the first step to obtain exactly SupportDerivedTensorNormalization for every pair of complexes.

For uniqueness, replace the second derived input by the functorial flat resolution of a complex representative. Its image under r is K-flat because r preserves flat objects and colimits. The target localization tensor map is thus invertible, as are both exact-functor factorization maps. Cancel these maps in the two normalization squares to identify the comparison components on this pair of representatives. Essential surjectivity of Q and naturality transport the equality to arbitrary derived inputs, proving uniqueness of the entire family. No additional hypothesis on the morphism or on either input is used.

lean.statement: def supportDerivedTensorComparison {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : SupportDerivedTensorComparisonFamily Λ f
lean.note: The ordinary comparison is chosen from its unique balanced-generator characterization; the derived comparison is chosen from its unique full naturality/total-complex characterization. Both definitions have real data from uniqueness assertions. The exact alpha-transport isomorphism and existing small-colimit and total-tensor-existence instances are exported. No arbitrary isomorphism is chosen and no hypothesis on f or the derived inputs is added.
